design.md's current REQ-004 'Signer output contract' requires generate-approval-sidecar.py (T-003's deliverable) to resolve weakening_verdict/predecessor_context_sha256/approval_epoch before signing, and REQ-006 states explicitly: 'generate-approval-sidecar.py and validate-approval-sidecar.py never accept a pre-computed weakening verdict as an input flag/file ... each invokes detect-policy-weakening.py itself, in-process ... at generation time and validation time respectively.' These fields are schema-required in design.md's approval-sidecar.schema.json. This makes T-003 functionally dependent on T-005's detect-policy-weakening.py, yet tasks.md T-003's Depends On / ### Blockers cite only T-002, and T-003's own Out of Scope explicitly disclaims it: 'The two-person/cooldown verdict's own computation (T-005; this task only ACCEPTS a verdict it is given and embeds it, it does not compute one).' T-003 is scheduled via the numeric-order chain to run before T-005 exists (T-003 to T-004 to T-005). No later task's Planned Files claims ownership of wiring this live call either: T-006, the only later task sharing REQ-004 per traceability.md's Task Mapping ('REQ-004 (share - recomputes T-003's construction)'), lists only validate-approval-sidecar.py/.sh/.ps1 in its Planned Files (not generate-approval-sidecar.py) even though T-006's Scope is assigned TEST-019, which asserts generate-approval-sidecar.py's own refusal behavior (acceptance-tests.md AC-019). This is a missing-blocker gap whose omission risks integration failure: T-003 could be marked Implementation Complete while generate-approval-sidecar.py still only accepts an externally-supplied verdict, directly contradicting design.md's current anti-tamper requirement. Because this design.md provenance-binding language was added/revised through the impl-review gate after task-review attempt-1 passed while T-003's tasks.md text is unchanged, this is a genuine new cross-artifact inconsistency exposed by this re-review, not a re-raised finding on unchanged content, so the post-implementation provenance re-review convergence rule does not apply.
